sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Dobharchú, sometimes written Dobharchu and also called Dorraghow, Dobhau, or Otter King, is an Irish folk being. This unsleeping king of otters, striped black and white, hunted and killed humans. Silver bullets alone could slay him. The hunt proved dangerous, and a successful hunter often died within a day. A piece of his hide kept its holder from drowning. Merchants sold bits of ordinary otter fur to sailors who feared death by water. Several families claimed descent from otters, most notably the McMurrows.

okr.objective: Document the supernatural Irish king otter Dobharchú and his lore.
